title: Bringing to repentance and generating living faith suffices—no separate temporal absolving sentence required
source_text: XIV. Proinde ut peccata homini remittantur, & ab iis censeatur apud Deum absolutus, ac Deo reconciliatus, sufficit ut Deus per gratiam suam peccatorem ad veram poenitentiam adducat, illique fidem vivam & efficacem ingeneret. Hoc enim posito, statim cessat homo obnoxius esse maledictioni & irae divinae, & incipit esse Deo gratus & acceptus ad vitam aeternam, vi alterius illius jam memoratae legis ab aeterno a Deo sancitae. Nec opus est praeterea alia quadam Dei actione, per quam remissio peccatorum in homine producatur proxime & immediate: aut ut Deus in tempore sententiam quandam pronuntiet, per quam peccator iste in singulari declaretur a Deo absolutus, & in gratiam a Deo receptus. Nec enim talis sententia magis necessaria est, ut homo apud Deum reus esse desinat, quam opposita quadam sententia opus est, ut homo post peccatum admissum, apud Deum reus poenae aeternae fiat. Cum ad utrumque abunde satis sit aeternum Dei decretum circa tum peccatores, tum poenitentes & fideles constitutum, & Evangelio solenniter promulgatum.
pass_a_gloss: Accordingly, for sins to be remitted to a man, and for him to be reckoned before God absolved from them and reconciled to God, it suffices that God through his grace bring the sinner to true repentance and generate in him a living and efficacious faith. For this being posited, the man at once ceases to be liable to the curse and divine wrath, and begins to be pleasing to God and accepted unto eternal life, by force of that other already-mentioned law sanctioned by God from eternity. Nor is there need further of some other action of God through which the remission of sins is produced in the man proximately and immediately; or that God in time pronounce some sentence through which that sinner in particular is declared absolved by God and received into grace by God. For such a sentence is no more necessary for the man to cease to be guilty before God than an opposite sentence is needed for the man, after sin admitted, to become guilty of eternal punishment before God—since for both the eternal decree of God constituted concerning both sinners and the penitent and faithful, and solemnly promulgated in the Gospel, is abundantly enough.
pass_b_english: Grace that brings true repentance and living faith is enough for actual absolution and reconciliation.
No extra temporal courtroom sentence—any more than guilt needed a fresh condemning sentence.

choices.why: Denies need for a further producing act beyond repentance/faith.
